e-6166.knowledge_point: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix
e-6166.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/a29e80b35c9505ee665a109978de9b936ee7ce59eef631d7af9a4b7954bd8696.png)
e-6166.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd and $4$th rows of $A$ are $-1$, $-4$ and $8$, respectively.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/d2f89fe83787daf667e01fd4c4fe644bc36cfe23b046088c22e8de17bb02dc28.png)

So, the answer is $-1+(-4)+8=3.$

e-4688.knowledge_point: Identifying Matrices in Row Echelon Form
e-4688.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

e-4687.knowledge_point: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form

Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

Which of the following matrices are not in row echelon form?

A=[603000510003],B=[1034−20000000144],C=[00000−10−10407000].

a
B only

EXPLANATION

Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

  1. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.
  2. Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.
With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

  • The matrix A is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied). A=[603000510003]

  • The matrix B is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated). B=[1034−20000000144]

  • The matrix C is not in row echelon form since the leading entry c32≠0 (condition II is violated). C=[00000−10−10407000]

Therefore, only B and C are not in row echelon form.

content.problem:
Which of the following matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the second row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry ${c}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $B$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.

Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form? A=[23−71043−400−25],B=[31−3103020000],C=[00220−402−1232].

C only
b
A and B only
c

d
A and C only
e

Submit

EXPLANATION

Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

  1. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.
  2. Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.
With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

  • The matrix A is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied). A=[23−71043−400−25]

  • The matrix B is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied). B=[31−3103020000]

  • The matrix C is not in row echelon form since c22≠0 (condition II is violated). C=[00220−402−1232]

Therefore, only A and B are in row echelon form.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form
content.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -7 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -7 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since ${c}_{22}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $B$ are in row echelon form.
